15.1.crux: Lightning is a giant electric spark, the same kind of thing as the tiny sparks you sometimes see when you take off a sweater.

cards.title: A huge spark

cols.head: Small spark
cells: Taking off a woollen sweater in the dark

say: Both are caused by electric charges.
Lightning is just the same thing on a gigantic scale.

cards.title: Franklin's discovery

steps.text: Long ago, people feared lightning and didn't know its cause
In 1752, Benjamin Franklin flew a kite in a thunderstorm and showed lightning is electric
Now we know how lightning forms and how to stay safe

say: Franklin showed that lightning and the spark from your clothes are the same kind of thing.

cards.title: An old observation
say: People have noticed charged objects for thousands of years.

crux_points: Lightning is an electric spark on a huge scale.
Benjamin Franklin showed lightning is electric.
Sparks from clothes are the same kind of thing, much smaller.

quiz.why: Lightning is an electric discharge, a spark on a huge scale.

quiz.q: Who showed that lightning is electrical?
quiz.why: Benjamin Franklin did this with his famous kite experiment.

15.2.crux: Rubbing two objects together can give them an electric charge, and charged objects attract small, light things.

cards.title: Try it yourself

steps.text: Rub a plastic comb in your dry hair, or a refill with polythene
It becomes charged
Bring it near tiny bits of paper: they jump up to it

say: Objects that get charges by rubbing are called charged objects.
The charges are called electric charges.

cards.title: What can be charged?
say: Rub different things and test them on bits of paper.

cards.title: Static charges

items.sub: Stays on the object, doesn't flow

say: Charges made by rubbing stay where they are: they are static charges.
When charges move, they make an electric current.

crux_points: Rubbing can give objects an electric charge.
Charged objects attract light objects like bits of paper.
Charges that stay in place are static; moving charges form a current.

quiz.q: A balloon rubbed on hair sticks to a wall because…
quiz.why: Rubbing charges the balloon, and charged objects attract other things.

quiz.q: Charges that do not move are called…
quiz.why: Static means not moving; moving charges are a current.

15.3.crux: There are two kinds of charge, positive and negative; like charges repel each other and unlike charges attract.

cards.title: Two kinds of charge
say: By convention, the charge on a glass rod rubbed with silk is called positive.
The other kind is called negative.

cards.title: Attract or repel?
say: Two balloons rubbed with the same cloth carry the same charge, so they push each other away.
cards.remember: Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.

cards.title: Balloon experiment

steps.text: Rub two balloons with a woollen cloth
Hang them near each other
They move apart: same charges repel

say: Repulsion is the sure test that two objects have the same charge.

crux_points: Charges are of two kinds: positive and negative.
Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.
A glass rod rubbed with silk is positively charged.

quiz.q: Two charged balloons push away from each other. Their charges are…
A positive charge and a negative charge will…

15.4.crux: Charge can move from one object to another through a metal; an electroscope shows this, and passing charge to the earth is called earthing.

cards.title: The electroscope
say: Touch the clip with a charged object.
Charge moves through the metal to both foil strips. Same charge on both → they repel and spread apart.

cards.title: Earthing

steps.text: Foil strips are spread apart (charged)
Touch the clip with your hand
The charge flows through your body into the earth
The strips collapse: they have lost their charge

say: Transferring charge to the earth is called earthing.
Buildings have earthing to protect us from shocks if electricity leaks.

cards.title: Discharge

items.sub: A huge discharge between clouds and earth

say: Next, we'll see how lightning is a massive discharge.

crux_points: Charge can be transferred through metals.
An electroscope's strips spread apart when charged (like charges repel).
Earthing passes charge safely into the earth.

quiz.q: What is marked '?' in the electroscope?
options: Foil strips, spread apart by like charges
quiz.why: The foil strips get the same charge and repel each other.

quiz.q: When you touch a charged electroscope, the strips collapse because…
options: The charge flows through you to the earth
quiz.why: This is earthing: the charge goes to the earth.

15.5.crux: In a thunderstorm, moving air and water separate charges: negative charges gather at the bottom of clouds and positive charges near the ground, until a giant spark, lightning, jumps between them.

cards.title: Charges in a storm cloud

labels.name: Positive charges
labels.note: Collect near the top of the cloud

labels.name: Lightning
labels.note: Charges meet in a giant spark

say: During a thunderstorm, air currents move up and water droplets move down.
These strong movements separate the charges.

cards.title: Step by step

steps.text: Air rushes up, water drops fall down
Charges separate: + at the top of the cloud, – at the bottom
Positive charges gather near the ground below
When too much charge builds up, air can't hold it back: a flash of lightning
The huge heat makes the air expand: we hear thunder

say: This sudden flow of charge is called an electric discharge.
cards.remember: Lightning = electric discharge between cloud and ground (or between clouds).

cards.title: Light before sound

cols.head: Thunder
cells: Sound travels slower, so it arrives later

say: That's why we see the flash first and hear thunder afterwards.

crux_points: Air currents and water drops separate charges in storm clouds.
Negative charges gather at the bottom of clouds; positive charges near the ground.
When the build-up is huge, a discharge (lightning) occurs.

quiz.q: Which charges collect at the bottom of a thundercloud?
quiz.why: Negative charges gather near the lower edge of the cloud.

quiz.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
options: Light travels much faster than sound
quiz.why: Both happen together, but light reaches us far sooner than sound.

15.6.crux: No open place is safe in lightning: go inside a building or a closed car, avoid tall trees and open fields, and if caught outside, squat low.

cards.title: Safe and unsafe places

cols.head: Safer
cells: Inside a car or bus with windows and doors shut
Under shorter trees in a forest

say: When you hear thunder, rush to a safer place.
Wait a while after the last thunder before going out again.

cards.title: Caught in the open?

steps.text: Stay away from trees and poles
Do NOT lie flat on the ground
Squat low, hands on your knees, head between your hands

say: Squatting makes you the smallest possible target.

cards.title: Indoors too

items.text: Avoid corded phones and metal pipes

say: Lightning can travel through wires and pipes into a house.

cards.title: Lightning conductor
say: A lightning conductor gives the charge an easy, safe path into the earth.
Metal columns, wiring and water pipes in buildings also help protect us to some extent.

crux_points: Shelter in a building or a closed car; avoid open fields, tall trees and high places.
If caught outside, squat low with your head between your hands; don't lie down.
Lightning conductors carry the discharge safely to the earth.

quiz.q: Where is it safest during a thunderstorm?
quiz.why: Buildings and closed cars give the best protection.

quiz.q: Which part of the lightning conductor is marked '?'
quiz.why: The tall metal rod catches the lightning and carries it to the earth.

15.7.crux: Earthquakes are sudden shakes of the ground caused by movements of huge plates deep in the Earth's crust; they can't be predicted, so we must build safely and know what to do.

cards.title: Why the ground shakes

labels.name: Plate
labels.note: The Earth's outer layer is broken into plates

say: When plates brush past, collide or slide under one another, the crust is disturbed.
We feel this disturbance as an earthquake.

cards.title: Measuring earthquakes

items.sub: Records the shaking as wavy lines

say: The Bhuj (2001) and Kashmir (2005) earthquakes were stronger than 7.5.
The scale isn't simple counting: magnitude 6 carries about 1000 times the destructive energy of magnitude 4.

cards.title: Danger zones in India
say: Earthquakes are more likely near plate boundaries, called seismic or fault zones.

cards.title: Stay safe

cols.head: Indoors
cells: Take shelter under a strong table
Stay away from tall, heavy furniture
If in bed, stay there and cover your head with a pillow

cols.head: Outdoors
cells: Away from buildings, trees and power lines

say: In a car or bus, stay inside and drive slowly to a clear spot.
cards.remember: Earthquakes can't be predicted, so be prepared.

cards.title: Build to resist

items.sub: Mud or timber better than heavy materials in danger zones

say: Most injuries come from falling objects and collapsing buildings.

crux_points: Earthquakes are caused by moving plates in the Earth's crust.
They are measured by a seismograph and on the Richter scale; they can't be predicted.
Build resistant structures; indoors shelter under a table, outdoors move to a clear spot.

options: Movement of plates in the Earth's crust
quiz.why: Plates moving past or into each other disturb the crust.

quiz.q: During an earthquake indoors, you should…
options: Take shelter under a strong table
quiz.why: A strong table protects you from falling objects.
A seismograph records the tremors as wavy lines.
